title: Coefficient coordinates for raw homogeneous ideal multiplication
statement: Let j:Z→X be a closed immersion, L an invertible module, J=ker j with J²=0, n,e≥0, D=canonicalTensorBoundaryComparisons(j,L,J²=0,n), and f:O_Z→(j*L)^n [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. Put F=j*(J tensor L^n), N=(j*L)^n, d=n(e+1), a=n(0+1), t=n((e+1)+1), and h:d+a=t. For s=tensorPowSection(f,1) ≫ (D.a 0).inv, the explicit raw multiplication m=tensorIdealSectionMultiply(j,L,a,d,t,h,s) [lem-sc-tensor-homogeneous-kernel-action] equals boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso_e.hom ≫ mulTensorPowSection(f,F,e,1) ≫ boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso_(e+1).inv as maps j*(J tensor L^d)→j*(J tensor L^t). This is an equality on Z before pushforward or passage to kernels, independent of any graded presentation or action.

proof.text: Use hD to replace D by canonicalTensorBoundaryComparisons. Expand boundarySectionDegreeIso as boundaryPullbackPowIso followed by tensorPowMulIso. Expand boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso into its pullback of the tensor-power regrouping and associator, its pullback tensorator, and its tensor-power pullback comparison. Expand tensorIdealSectionMultiply as its explicit composite. Only module tensor maps occur.

Naturality of the pullback tensorator moves the section through the tensor comparison. The degree-one tensorPowSection f 1 includes the inverse right unitor, which cancels the degree-one tensor-power regrouping. On the coefficient side, keep the ideal factor fixed, group the first n copies with it, group the remaining factors into e blocks of n, and append one further block through f. These are the same ordered factors as raw ideal multiplication. The regrouping identity follows by induction on tensor-power exponents: addition associativity is induction on the first exponent, with the pentagon in the successor case; multiplication regrouping respects addition by induction on the number of blocks using that identity. The analogous pullback regrouping is induction on the exponent using tensorator naturality and associativity. The zero cases are the unit comparisons and triangle identity. This proves the displayed equality of composites, with no invertibility assumption on the ideal.

The output-degree equality h is the arithmetic identity n(e+1)+n=n(e+2). All transports of that equality agree by proof irrelevance. Thus the comparison holds also at n=0 and e=0. The proof uses no graded algebra presentation, quotient action or cohomology.

theorem tensorIdealSectionMultiply_coefficient_comparison {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) (n : ℕ) (D : TensorBoundaryComparisonData j L n)
    (hD : canonicalTensorBoundaryComparisons j L hI n = D) (e : ℕ)
    (f : 𝟙_ Z.Modules ⟶ ((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n)
    (h : n * (e + 1) + n * (0 + 1) = n * ((e + 1) + 1)) :
    tensorIdealSectionMultiply j L (n * (0 + 1)) (n * (e + 1))
        (n * ((e + 1) + 1)) h (tensorPowSection f 1 ≫ (D.a 0).inv) =
      (boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n e).hom ≫
        mulTensorPowSection f ((tensorPullback j).obj
          (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow n)) e 1 ≫
        (boundaryCoefficientDegreeIso j L n (e + 1)).inv
